property_statement: No consensus property violation was established from the inspected executable source in this run.
summary: Inspected the core term/election handling, leader/follower step functions, commit and append logic, log/unstable storage transitions, Ready/Advance and async-storage interfaces, quorum vote counting, progress tracking, and read-index handling. Candidate hypotheses involving lease-based read responses, self-vote durability, unstable-log ABA protection, and snapshot restores were formed and checked against the source. In each case, either the code contains a guard or ordering that prevents the hypothesized violation (e.g., vote and append responses are deferred until durable state, unstable-log responses are term-filtered, commitTo refuses to advance beyond lastIndex, and read responses are withheld until a current-term commit), or the remaining hazard depends on caller obligations or clock assumptions that are outside the library boundary and fault model. No decisive ordering, guard, threshold, or state relation linking an inspected mechanism to a protocol-property contradiction could be established, so no candidate met the evidentiary threshold.
uncertainties: Execution and fault-injection harnesses were unavailable, so reachability of any hypothesized interleaving could not be confirmed.

Several liveness- and availability-sensitive paths depend on caller-furnished Tick scheduling, Storage durability behavior, and Ready/Advance ordering, which are caller obligations under the target boundary.

The suspension criteria were applied strictly: source comments and tests were not treated as executable proof, and no inspected code path yielded a confirmed decisive relation to a protocol property violation.
